answer: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard introduced by Anthropic that lets LLM applications connect to external tools and data sources through a uniform JSON-RPC interface.

results.title: Model Context Protocol - Introduction
results.content: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open protocol that standardizes how applications provide context to large language models (LLMs). Think of MCP like a USB-C port for AI applications: just as USB-C provides a standardized way to connect devices to various peripherals, MCP provides a standardized way to connect AI models to different data sources and tools. MCP follows a client-host-server architecture and uses JSON-RPC 2.0 messages over stdio or streamable HTTP.

results.title: Specification - Model Context Protocol (2025-03-26)
results.content: This specification defines the Model Context Protocol revision 2025-03-26. It covers the base protocol, the message framing used by each transport, the lifecycle (initialise, operation, shutdown) and the server features: resources, prompts and tools. Clients and servers MUST negotiate a protocol version during initialisation.

results.title: Introducing the Model Context Protocol
results.content: Today we are open-sourcing the Model Context Protocol (MCP), a new standard for connecting AI assistants to the systems where data lives, including content repositories, business tools and development environments. Early adopters include Block, Apollo, Zed, Replit, Codeium and Sourcegraph.
